details: Tokenizes the document, builds a small AST (tables, arrays of tables, key/value pairs), normalises the spacing, the indentation and the quote style of the keys and values and prints the formatted TOML, with the formatting rules held in ``FormatConfig``.

tcg3.py.summary: Create a Termux-shebanged symlink in ``~/bin`` from clipboard or file content.
details: Reads the script path or the source text from the clipboard, detects the interpreter (python or bash), adds the Termux shebang to the first line and links or writes the script into ``~/bin``, ``~/bashbin`` or ``~/.local/bin``.

tchat2json.py.summary: Convert a chat export into JSON, CSV or SQLite.
details: Parses the ``[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] user: message`` lines into per-user message groups, optionally merges consecutive messages of the same user or removes the timestamps, and writes the chosen output format.

tcleaner.py.summary: Free space on a Termux install.
details: The ``termux`` subcommand strips the man/info/doc pages and the locales, adds a dpkg config that keeps them from coming back and clears the caches; ``junk`` deletes the junk names listed in ``/sdcard/data/junk`` under ``$HOME`` and ``pycache`` removes the bytecode caches. ``--dry-run`` previews the deletions.

tell_font_name.py.summary: Print the family names of the given font files and rename them accordingly.
details: Reads the name table with fontTools, picks the best family/subfamily combination, sanitises it into a file-name-safe string and renames the font file to ``<family>-<style>.ttf``.

ter_ser.py.summary: Minify JavaScript files in place with terser.
details: Runs ``terser --compress --mangle`` over the ``.js``/``.jsx``/``.jsm``/``.jsc`` files, skipping the ones that are already ``.min.js`` or the notebook bundles, and prints the size reduction for each of them in parallel.

termimg0.py.summary: Print an image in the terminal with half-block characters.
details: Resizes the image to the terminal width, samples the pixels in pairs and renders each one as a ``▀`` glyph whose foreground and background are 24-bit colours.

textclean.py.summary: Clean text files with a set of dedicated subcommands.
details: Subcommands: ``empty-lines`` drops the blank lines, ``invisible`` strips the non-printable characters, ``pattern`` removes a multi-line pattern (read from ``/sdcard/lic`` or given inline), ``lines`` removes the lines matching substrings or regexes, ``header`` removes the ``# Author/# Email/# Time`` header and ``json-fields`` renames the JSON keys to ``field_1``, ``field_2``... ``--dry-run`` and ``--no-backup`` control the writes.

Subcommands: ``clean`` removes the zero-width and exotic space characters, ``normalize-lines`` trims and normalises each line, ``norm-white`` collapses the whitespace and ``reformat-text``/``reformatext`` rewraps the paragraphs to the configured maximum line length, splitting the long sentences at punctuation.

tnn.py.summary: Replace the tabs of text files with four spaces.
details: Walks the given paths (or all non-binary files below the current directory), rewrites the files that contain a tab and reports the ones that were updated.

to.env.py.summary: Extract the API tokens from a project README into ``tokens.txt`` and ``.env`` files.
details: Matches the ``model: token`` pairs of the README against the known model names, maps each model to its environment variable and writes the collected tokens to ``tokens.txt`` plus one ``.env`` per destination.

to_jpg.py.summary: Convert the PNG/WebP/BMP/TIFF/GIF images below the current directory to JPEG.
details: Flattens the transparency on white, saves each image as a quality-70 ``.jpg`` next to the original and deletes the source; existing ``.jpg`` targets are skipped and the run ends with the converted/error counts.
to_jpg.py.notes: Destructive: the original images are removed after conversion, so back them up first.

to_unicode.py.summary: Turn the ``\xNN`` escapes of a file into real characters.
details: Reads the file (UTF-8, falling back to latin-1), replaces every ``\xNN`` sequence with the matching character and writes the result back.

Accepts file paths, shell globs and a ``-f LISTFILE`` with one pattern per line, resolves the matches, gives a unique name to the collisions and moves each file into ``~/.local/bin``, printing the new names.
